6. A native counterexample rules out independent component refinement

The missing correlations cannot simply be dropped.

Take an allowed nearest-neighbour path with $r$ edges,

$$H=J\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}X_jX_{j+1},
\qquad \eta=0,$$

with rational $J,\gamma>0$, all-site native depolarization, initial $|0\cdots0\rangle$, and computational readout.

Let $p_{ab}(t)$ be the probability that the endpoint bits are $a,b$ and every interior bit is zero. Then

$$D_r(t):=p_{00}p_{11}-p_{01}p_{10}
=
J^{2r}t^{2r}+O(t^{2r+1}).
\tag{24}$$

This statement retains $\gamma>0$. A concise proof is available:

- Give each edge its own $J_j$. Cutting any edge makes the two sides independent, so $D_r=0$.

- Conjugating $Z$ on one side of an edge changes only that $J_j$’s sign while preserving preparation, measurement and noise.

- Every nonzero Taylor monomial therefore contains $\prod_jJ_j^2$.

- At total degree $2r$, no factor of $\gamma$ can occur. The coefficient can be computed at $\gamma=0$, where it equals $\prod_jJ_j^2$.

An explicit remainder estimate makes the sign certified. With

$$\Lambda=2rJ+2(r+1)\gamma,$$

choose rational $t>0$ satisfying

$$t\le
\min\!\left\{
\frac1{2\Lambda},
\frac{J^{2r}(2r+1)!}{24(2\Lambda)^{2r+1}}
\right\}.
\tag{25}$$

Then

$$D_r(t)\ge\tfrac12J^{2r}t^{2r}>0.
\tag{26}$$

Now consider the rule that samples the exact coarse record, groups holes at distance at most $R$, and samples the true conditional marginal of each component independently.

Set $r=R+1$. For the original output

$$x_*=(1,0,\ldots,0,1),$$

both endpoints must be holes. Any interior hole joins the endpoints into one component, so those coarse records are refined exactly. The only erroneous compatible mask has endpoint holes and every interior zero revealed.

Writing

$$Z_\theta=\theta^2p_{00}
+\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11},$$

the resulting unconditional error is

$$\boxed{
P(x_*)-Q(x_*)
=
\frac{(1-\theta)^{r-1}\theta^2D_r(t)}{Z_\theta}
>0.
}
\tag{27}$$

Thus the discrepancy persists after discarding the artificial mask. The report also gives a full-square padding construction.
